candidates.label: Lycaonia (label point)
candidates.support: Lycaonia's identity as the region containing Lystra and Derbe is undisputed. The label point is Wikidata's point for the region; Pleiades independently records the region under the same name, citing Cicero and Strabo, though without a coordinate of its own.

summary.text: Lycaonia was a plain in the central-southern part of Asia Minor. Acts records that after Paul and Barnabas were driven out of Iconium, they 'fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra, Derbe, and the surrounding region,' where the residents spoke 'the speech of Lycaonia.' This project's Lycaonia record reflects the western, Roman part of the region, where Lystra and Derbe lay.

history.text: The International Standard Bible Encyclopedia explains that in Paul's time, Lycaonia 'consisted of two parts, a western and an eastern. The western part was a "region" or subdivision of the Roman province Galatia; the eastern was called Lycaonia Antiochiana, after Antiochus of Commagene under whom it had been placed in 37 AD.' Acts 14:6, naming only Lystra and Derbe, describes the western, Roman part of Lycaonia, which is the sense this project's record follows; the eastern, non-Roman portion lay outside the province at this project's about AD 50 date.

scripture.textWEB: they became aware of it and fled to the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra, Derbe, and the surrounding region.
When the multitude saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voice, saying in the language of Lycaonia, “The gods have come down to us in the likeness of men!”
